date.note: Commons supplies 2012, while the upstream collection describes completion of the Musopen public-domain release project in 2012. No Katz session date is separately established; the release year is not relabelled as a recording date.

place.note: The recording venue is not given; the performer’s residence or institutional affiliation is not used as a session place.

label.note: Musopen is the recording-release project; no original commercial carrier label is established.

catalogue.note: No original carrier catalogue number is supplied.

matrixTakeSides.note: No matrix, take, side or original recording-medium identification is supplied; inapplicability is not inferred from a digital file.

credits.note: No transfer or mastering engineer is named. The repository uploader is not automatically a transfer engineer.

date.note: No transfer date is established; publication and repository upload dates are distinct from transfer dates.

processing.value: FLAC collection redistributed through Commons, with a Wikimedia MP3 access derivative.
processing.note: The upstream item describes FLAC encoding at 32 bits per sample; this is an encoding claim, not evidence of 32-bit original capture. Editing and mastering history are not identified.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source FLAC

composition.value: Underlying composition is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms.
composition.note: Bach died in 1750. This does not clear a separately protected modern performing edition.

recording.value: Rule 1 — explicit public-domain recording release by Musopen (Commons PD-author).
recording.note: The opened file-description wikitext distinguishes recording={{PD-author|Musopen}} from the separate composition-only PD-old-auto-expired tag. The upstream collection explicitly says the project purchased and released recordings to the public domain, including the Goldberg Variations; its Public Domain Mark alone is not the basis.

rights.creditLine: Johann Sebastian Bach, Goldberg Variations, opening Aria; Shelley Katz, piano. Musopen public-domain recording release, distributed through Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons. Session date and place unknown; streamed without editorial audio edits.
